paragraphs: Give the system its own attributable identity

An accounting agent should act as a non-human workload with an identifiable owner, workflow, environment, and permission set. It should not borrow a person's session, API key, mailbox, signer credential, or approval authority.
Workload identity
Identifies the deployed service, agent, and environment for every request.
Human identity
Identifies the requester, reviewer, approver, or operator and their current authority.
Workflow identity
Binds activity to an approved objective, version, entity, period, and run.
Tool identity
Identifies the constrained interface and records the policy decision for each call.
A model is not a principal
The surrounding system authenticates the workload, assigns scope, evaluates policy, and records the actor. Never treat fluent text as proof of identity, permission, or approval.

Authorize every tool call
Authenticate.Verify workload and human identities using current, non-shared credentials.
Bind context.Attach workflow, run, entity, period, purpose, data classification, and requested action.
Evaluate policy.Check allowed tool, fields, records, amount, time, authority level, and segregation conflicts.
Verify approval.For A3, authenticate the approver and match the exact, unexpired payload.
Execute narrowly.Use field-level permissions, idempotency, transaction limits, and deny-by-default behavior.
Record and reconcile.Log the decision and result, compare it with the approved intent, and route differences.
The prompt is not the policy engine
A prompt may explain the rule to the model. Only deterministic authorization can reliably enforce identity, scope, amount, approval state, payload integrity, and prohibited actions.
Preserve segregation of duties

Agents can collapse roles accidentally when a single tool bundle can request, maintain master data, approve, execute, reconcile, and delete evidence. Map incompatible responsibilities at the action level and enforce them across human and non-human identities.Segregation-of-duties conflicts and enforcement examples
| Responsibility | Conflict to prevent | Example enforcement
| Request | Requesting and approving the same action | Independent approver role and policy decision
| Master data | Changing beneficiary data and releasing payment | Separate tools, identities, and verification evidence
| Preparation | Preparing and finally approving accounting work | Named reviewer with no model-delegated approval
| Execution | Executing and concealing an unauthorized effect | Immutable logs and independent reconciliation
| Assessment | Performing a control and assessing its own effectiveness | Independent human evaluator and retained exceptions

Classify data before use and restrict collection to the approved accounting purpose.
Prefer scoped connectors or short-lived tokens over copied credentials and broad exports.
Minimize fields, redact unnecessary personal data, and isolate entities and environments.
Define provider use, location, retention, training, subprocessors, export, and deletion terms.
Keep secrets out of prompts, traces, workpapers, evaluation sets, and reviewer packets.
Honor accounting-record retention, privacy obligations, investigations, and legal holds together.
Test revocation, tool denial, provider outage, compromise, data export, and exit procedures.

Production begins when real users, records, decisions, or actions can depend on the workflow. Before that point, assign owners, freeze the approved version, test failure paths, and prove that the team can deny, pause, recover, and reconcile the system.
Accounting, system, control, security, vendor, and incident owners are named.
The approved workflow, authority matrix, tools, data, limits, and evaluation results are versioned.
Write paths are least-privilege, approval-bound, idempotent, observable, and independently reconciled.
Alerts have thresholds, an on-call owner, response time, escalation path, and pause action.
Run records, workpapers, approvals, receipts, and source versions meet retention requirements.
Fallback, provider outage, credential revocation, rollback, correction, and exit procedures have been exercised.
Monitor accounting outcomes and system behaviorProduction monitoring signals and required responses
| Signal family | Examples | Response
| Population | Untied totals, exclusions, duplicates, incomplete runs | Stop the run; re-establish source completeness
| Quality | Calculation error, unsupported claim, missed exception, rising reviewer rework | Limit scope; review affected outputs; add regression cases
| Authority | Tool denial, approval bypass, payload drift, self-approval, duplicate action | Pause write path immediately; preserve authorization evidence
| Accounting | Unreconciled effect, post-close adjustment, corrected filing, stale open item | Identify affected records; correct through authorized procedures
| Operations | Latency, timeout, retry loop, cost spike, unavailable provider, failed receipt | Degrade safely, fail closed, and invoke continuity plan
| Change | New model, prompt, policy, source, tool, schema, vendor, or jurisdiction | Reassess and rerun the applicable evaluation gate
Pause on control failure

If scope, approval, permission, completeness, payload integrity, or reconciliation cannot be established, fail closed and preserve the current state. Do not ask the model to reason around a failed control.

Treat behavior changes as production changes
Identify.Record the changed model, prompt, tool, source, policy, template, evaluator, infrastructure, or dependency.
Assess.Map affected workflows, assertions, actions, data, jurisdictions, controls, and retained work.

Approve.Record the accountable release decision, conditions, residual risk, timing, and rollback version.
Observe.Use heightened monitoring after release and compare quality, overrides, exceptions, and system behavior.
Use the production change record to preserve the decision and the evaluation plan to define the evidence needed for release.

Contain, preserve, determine, correct

LearnAdd regression cases, redesign the control, reassess risk, and require approval before resuming.
Record the event with the incident report. Never silently edit or delete the original run, approval, or accounting record.

Normal

paragraphs: Before the pilot

Assign a business owner, technical owner, control owner, and reviewer. Document the current process and collect a small set of representative, edge, contradictory, and known-answer cases.
The workflow has a defined objective and reviewer.
Source access is authorized and limited to the required data.
The team can reproduce control totals and key calculations.
The expected output and review standard are documented.
The system can stop without changing a record or sending a message.
The team can restore the prior configuration after a change.

Pilot stages
1
Choose the scope

Select one repeatable workflow with stable evidence and a named reviewer.
2
Write the specification

Define inputs, output, checks, authority limits, and stop conditions.
3
Run in shadow mode

Use read-only access beside the current process. Do not change records.
4
Prepare drafts

Let the agent prepare work. Require approval for judgments and external actions.
5
Measure the result

Track coverage, accuracy, exceptions, rework, cycle time, and reviewer overrides.
6
Set the next boundary
Expand only when the run record supports a wider scope or authority.
MeasuresMeasures for evaluating a supervised accounting-agent pilot
| Measure | Question
| Coverage | How much of the defined population did the run process?
| Accuracy | Did calculations, matches, classifications, and citations agree with known answers?
| Exception quality | Did the run find material problems without creating excessive false positives?
| Traceability | Can the reviewer follow each material result to its source and procedure?
| Rework | How much preparation and correction did the reviewer perform?
| Cycle time | How long did preparation, review, correction, and approval take?
| Overrides | Which agent recommendations did reviewers reject or change, and why?
Stop conditions

Pause the pilot and investigate when any of these conditions occur:
The source population cannot be tied to an authoritative control total.
The agent uses an unauthorized source or tool.
A material result lacks support or contradicts source evidence.
The system performs or attempts a prohibited action.
Reviewer overrides increase after a model, prompt, tool, or mapping change.
The run record cannot reproduce the result or identify the configuration used.
Expansion decision
Record the evidence that supports any wider scope, tool access, or action authority. Keep the current boundary when results remain mixed or the review burden offsets the time saved.

records.title: What establishes journal-extraction completeness?
records.summary: A bounded synthesis of endpoint-specific paging, ordering, changing-population, and journal-view evidence for evaluating whether an accounting extraction is complete.

provenance.review_scope: Cross-source synthesis of the linked record annotations and their stated limitations.
provenance.note: Editorial synthesis reviewed 2026-09-07. It is not professional accounting advice, a live extraction test, or proof that any population is complete.

data.title: What establishes journal-extraction completeness?
data.description: A bounded cross-source synthesis for designing and reviewing accounting journal extraction evidence.
data.intended_audience: Accounting data engineers, reviewers, and agent builders evaluating extraction evidence.

editorial_brief.question: What establishes journal-extraction completeness?
editorial_brief.answer: The checked sources support an endpoint-specific extraction protocol with a documented cursor or ordering rule, a termination condition, and reconciliation evidence. Paging mechanics alone do not establish completeness: Oracle warns that an updating population can change between requests, Xero withholds unreconciled bank-statement lines from public APIs, and SAP describes entry-view compression for some large documents. The result is a reviewable method and set of limitations, not a universal completeness guarantee.

findings.claim: Xero's journal endpoint documents a bounded page size, JournalNumber continuation, and continuation through an empty response even after a short page.
findings.qualification: This is publisher documentation; no tenant extraction or reconciliation was performed.

findings.claim: A completeness review must preserve endpoint-specific ordering and filtering assumptions rather than applying one generic incremental-retrieval rule.
findings.qualification: Xero's general retrieval advice distinguishes Journals from other endpoints; the sources do not prove a complete live population.

findings.claim: A changing source population can invalidate a simple page count or offset traversal as evidence of a stable snapshot.
findings.qualification: The Oracle contract is a general collection contract and does not establish the permissions or completeness of a particular financial resource.

findings.claim: A journal response cannot be treated as the complete unreconciled bank-statement population when the publisher says that data is not exposed through public APIs.
findings.qualification: The documented product boundary may change and was not tested against an authenticated integration.

findings.claim: Journal-entry and ledger views may represent different detail, including compression of specified item types for documents over 999 line items.
findings.qualification: This is a SAP posting-model description, not a universal extraction ceiling or a tested read-path reconciliation.

disagreements.claim: Offset traversal is prescribed for Xero Journals, while Oracle's general offset contract warns that updates between requests can change displayed records; these are different endpoint contracts rather than a resolved universal rule.
disagreements.qualification: The sources do not establish which strategy is appropriate for an unexamined endpoint.

unknowns: Whether a particular tenant extraction is complete without control totals, a stable snapshot, or a source-supported reconciliation.
Whether current product limits, permissions, and endpoint behavior match the checked documentation.

records.summary: A bounded synthesis separating task and model results from evidence about dependable accounting workflows, professional judgment, or current deployment reliability.

provenance.review_scope: Cross-source synthesis of the linked empirical and benchmark record annotations.
provenance.note: Editorial synthesis reviewed 2026-09-07. It does not establish professional validation, current model reliability, or deployment safety.

data.title: What do accounting LLM benchmarks demonstrate?
data.description: A bounded synthesis for interpreting accounting and financial-language-model benchmark evidence.
data.intended_audience: Researchers, accounting-agent builders, and reviewers interpreting benchmark results.

editorial_brief.question: What do accounting LLM benchmarks demonstrate?
editorial_brief.answer: The checked studies demonstrate performance on their named tasks, datasets, prompts, models, and grading procedures. They provide comparative evidence and useful failure modes, such as calculation errors, hallucination, label uncertainty, and information ceilings. They do not by themselves demonstrate dependable accounting workflows, professional judgment, live-system reliability, or transfer to current models and unseen populations.

findings.claim: A focused accounting-assistant experiment reports different results for case-based calculations and decisions, and associates calculation errors with misapplied accounting principles.
findings.qualification: The observations are across model variants and prompts, not 480 independent tasks; older models and a curated experiment limit transfer.

findings.claim: Tax-question experiments report effects from relevant legal text and few-shot prompting that vary by model and setting.
findings.qualification: The questions are generated multiple-choice items, grading uses known answers and model-based procedures, and no professional-lawyer baseline is established.

findings.claim: Financial-report hallucination assessment can measure masked-span recovery and answerability within a defined corpus, but that metric is narrower than autonomous accounting reliability.
findings.qualification: The project uses answerability checks and a pilot human audit; no independent replication was performed and filing rights remain separate.

findings.claim: A financial benchmark's reported comparison can be constrained by its information ceiling and possible label errors.
findings.qualification: The claim is limited to the evaluated binary tasks, models, dataset card warnings, and setup.

disagreements.claim: The checked studies use different task designs, datasets, graders, and metrics, so their numerical results are not directly comparable as one ranking of accounting ability.
disagreements.qualification: This is a scope mismatch across study designs, not evidence that one study is wrong.

unknowns: Whether any result transfers to a current production model, a particular accounting entity, or a controlled workflow.
How results change with independent professional grading, private tests, retrieval, tool use, and reviewer intervention.

provenance.review_scope: Cross-source synthesis of the linked dataset descriptions, rights annotations, and limitations.
provenance.note: Editorial synthesis reviewed 2026-09-07. Dataset suitability, rights, and professional use require source-specific verification.

data.title: How should financial datasets be chosen under provenance and rights limits?
data.description: A bounded dataset-selection brief for accounting-agent research.
data.intended_audience: Accounting researchers and agent builders selecting data for evaluation, prototyping, or reproducibility work.

editorial_brief.question: How should financial datasets be chosen under provenance and rights limits?
editorial_brief.answer: Start by naming the evidence object and the behavior the dataset can support: simulated transactions, application records, synthetic reviewer decisions, administrative reports, or award actions are not interchangeable with observed ledger or payment data. Then record generation or reporting provenance, labels and their limitations, population and time coverage, and the dataset-specific license. Repository code terms do not automatically grant rights to externally hosted data, and public availability does not prove representativeness or live accounting validity.

findings.claim: The IBM AML repository describes simulated payments, transfers, and purchases and separately identifies repository and dataset licenses.
findings.qualification: Simulated laundering labels are not independently observed banking outcomes; license terms must be read separately.

findings.claim: Synthetic card data can provide scale for research while leaving representativeness and dataset-specific permission unresolved.
findings.qualification: The checked external download documentation did not resolve a separate dataset permission grant.

findings.claim: Bank-account-fraud application datasets and synthetic-alert review resources describe different populations and different observation status.
findings.qualification: The reviewed reviewer decisions are simulated, and the upstream and derivative rights interaction was not resolved.

findings.claim: CMS cost reports and USAspending award transactions are administrative reporting or award-action data with defined fields and boundaries, not complete general ledgers or bank payments.
findings.qualification: Both sources retain publisher and reporting limitations; no download was independently reconciled.

disagreements.claim: A dataset may be useful for controlled task testing while being unsuitable as evidence of real-world financial behavior; usefulness and representativeness must be assessed separately.
disagreements.qualification: The sources describe different data-generating processes and cannot be collapsed into one evidence tier.

unknowns: Whether a selected dataset is current, complete, legally reusable for the intended purpose, or representative of the target workflow.
Whether labels reflect expert decisions, source-reported fields, simulated rules, or downstream annotation errors in the exact release used.

editorial_brief.answer: Separate book WIP from tax methods, then determine the contract category and taxable-year cohort. Read the enacted amendment together with method-change procedures. records.title: Foundations for accounting agent builders
records.summary: Twenty sources connecting professional duties, accounting evidence, controls, agent architecture, and human oversight.

provenance.note: Migrated from the existing project corpus. Import and integrity checks are not source verification or professional review.

data.selection_note: Reference bibliography extracted from the former core course. Course activities and progression were retired.

annotations.contribution: Professional duties, ethical principles, and rule applicability for AICPA members and engagements.
annotations.why_it_matters: An agent does not inherit professional standing, independence, judgment, or approval authority from the person or firm using it.
annotations.limitation: Applicability depends on membership, role, service, independence, jurisdiction, and effective interpretations.

annotations.contribution: The authoritative source of nongovernmental US GAAP recognition, measurement, presentation, and disclosure requirements.
annotations.why_it_matters: A model-generated treatment is not authoritative support; the applicable Codification text and facts remain the basis for the conclusion.
annotations.limitation: Basic access may not expose every research feature or historical version.

annotations.contribution: The official route to IFRS Accounting Standards and related issued material.
annotations.why_it_matters: Framework, jurisdiction, effective date, and access tier must be known before an agent can retrieve or cite applicable IFRS material.
annotations.limitation: Registration or subscription may be required, and the catalog does not reproduce licensed standard text.

annotations.contribution: A durable framework for control objectives, components, principles, information, communication, and monitoring.
annotations.why_it_matters: Agent controls must operate inside the entity's control system; a passing model evaluation does not establish control design or operating effectiveness.
annotations.limitation: The full framework and supporting tools may require purchase or permission; this catalog stores only metadata and original summaries.

annotations.contribution: A normative PCAOB account of audit-evidence sufficiency, appropriateness, relevance, reliability, and contradiction.
annotations.why_it_matters: The source makes visible why retrieved material, model confidence, and a clean narrative are not substitutes for appropriate evidence.
annotations.limitation: AS 1105 is binding within PCAOB audit scope; using it as an accounting-process design reference does not create an audit procedure or assurance conclusion.

annotations.contribution: A normative PCAOB baseline for reviewable documentation, attribution, completion, retention, and later changes.
annotations.why_it_matters: Tool traces can aid diagnosis, but they do not by themselves explain purpose, evidence, exceptions, judgment, review, and disposition.
annotations.limitation: AS 1215 governs PCAOB engagements and does not automatically set documentation rules for management accounting, tax, internal audit, or non-PCAOB assurance work.

annotations.contribution: A normative PCAOB source for top-down, risk-based ICFR audit work and the distinction between design and operating effectiveness.
annotations.why_it_matters: An agent can prepare evidence and tests, but management and auditor responsibilities, control conclusions, and applicable criteria remain distinct.
annotations.limitation: AS 2201 governs the auditor's integrated audit; management remains responsible for its assessment and system of internal control.

annotations.contribution: Professional guidance that frames generative and agentic AI use in audit through competence, skepticism, evidence, supervision, and documentation.
annotations.why_it_matters: It connects AI-specific operating questions to familiar audit responsibilities without treating an AI capability as audit evidence or an audit conclusion.
annotations.limitation: The primary audience is audit-firm central functions under the UK framework.

annotations.contribution: A foundational research pattern for interleaving language-model reasoning with actions in an external environment.
annotations.why_it_matters: It gives accountants a concrete picture of why an agent can choose tools and steps, while giving builders a baseline pattern whose accounting controls remain unspecified.
annotations.limitation: The paper studies general interactive tasks, not accounting accuracy, professional judgment, approval, or control effectiveness.

annotations.contribution: A voluntary, risk-based framework organized around govern, map, measure, and manage functions.
annotations.why_it_matters: It supplies a common risk vocabulary for owners, builders, and reviewers without replacing accounting frameworks, laws, or professional standards.
annotations.limitation: The AI RMF is voluntary general guidance and does not determine accounting treatment, audit compliance, or system effectiveness.

annotations.contribution: A companion risk profile for generative-AI risks and suggested actions across the AI lifecycle.
annotations.why_it_matters: It helps teams look beyond answer accuracy to provenance, confabulation, information integrity, misuse, privacy, and monitoring.
annotations.limitation: The profile is cross-sector guidance, not an accounting, audit, security-certification, or legal compliance determination.

annotations.contribution: A system-level account of data dependencies, feedback loops, undeclared consumers, configuration debt, and boundary erosion in machine-learning systems.
annotations.why_it_matters: Accounting agents inherit dependencies across ledgers, spreadsheets, close tools, workpapers, identities, and downstream reports that a successful demo can hide.
annotations.limitation: The paper predates modern language-model agents and offers qualitative engineering analysis rather than accounting outcome evidence.

annotations.contribution: A peer-reviewed critique and framework for evaluating agent systems with cost, reproducibility, holdouts, shortcuts, and downstream utility in view.
annotations.why_it_matters: It helps prevent one favorable run or a model-only score from becoming a broad claim about accounting-workflow value.
annotations.limitation: Its examples are general agent benchmarks rather than validated accounting workflows, control tests, or professional-review studies.

annotations.contribution: An accounting-native reconciliation benchmark that exposes multi-document evidence, ambiguity, and reliability limits.
annotations.why_it_matters: It supplies field-specific evidence that plausible language performance does not settle longer, evidence-linked accounting work.
annotations.limitation: The evidence is synthetic and benchmark-specific.

annotations.contribution: An exploratory research design for decomposing audit work across specialized agents and retained evidence.
annotations.why_it_matters: It is useful as an architecture hypothesis while making clear that orchestration does not confer audit authority or prove evidence sufficiency.
annotations.limitation: Working-paper status and an exploratory case limit evidentiary weight.

annotations.contribution: A research example of combining graph-grounded financial-reporting work with executable deterministic validation.
annotations.why_it_matters: Its ablation makes a concrete case for moving inspectable rule checks out of model judgment in a bounded structured-data task.
annotations.limitation: Preprint status and a 67-case derived sample limit generalization.

annotations.contribution: An official-staff experiment on how structured XBRL data and tool use affect model performance in financial and sustainability analysis.
annotations.why_it_matters: It gives readers a bounded example of how information structure and tools can change performance without proving a production accounting outcome.
annotations.limitation: The experiment is an official staff study in selected analysis tasks, not a general result for ledgers, controls, audit evidence, or production systems.

annotations.contribution: Official financial-sector risk guidance on generative and agentic AI implications for technology, cyber security, and operational resilience.
annotations.why_it_matters: It demonstrates how a regulator frames ownership, access, concentration, monitoring, and resilience without certifying a specific product or accounting workflow.
annotations.limitation: The bulletin is not an accounting or auditing standard.

annotations.contribution: First-party documentation of AI-supported close, reconciliation, flux, and EPM capabilities for a named release.
annotations.why_it_matters: It teaches readers to convert provider feature language into a testable local diligence question rather than an effectiveness or ROI claim.
annotations.limitation: The article is product-direction material and disclaims any delivery commitment; availability can vary by edition, module, account, region, and release state.

annotations.contribution: First-party release documentation for close monitoring, reconciliation assistance, permissions, dependencies, and regional limits.
annotations.why_it_matters: Paired with another provider record, it shows how superficially similar product claims can differ in scope, dependencies, and test requirements.
annotations.limitation: The record documents a specific 2025 release and supported regions.
